extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of coal combustion residual (CCR) surface impoundments, State and federal permitting authorities, environmental consultants, and facility engineers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and regulatory requirements for evaluating, documenting, and implementing closure and post-closure of legacy CCR (coal combustion residual) surface impoundments under 40 CFR part 257, including conditions for deferral, deadlines, required plans, monitoring, and permitting equivalency determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure equivalency determination (deferral to permitting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the facility was subject to standards different than the Federal CCR closure standards (e.g., closure as part of a CERCLA cleanup or State order) but otherwise equivalent in mitigating risks, the requirement to meet §257.102 standards will be deferred to permitting, where a closure equivalency determination will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will defer evaluation of potentially equivalent closures to the permit authority, which will determine equivalency through the permit application review. CERCLA and RCRA subtitle C responses are likely to be consistent with §257.102, but small variations may exist and will require review rather than a blanket exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic exemption for State-authorized closures (RCRA §4005(d) process required)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA disagrees that legacy CCR surface impoundments should be exempted merely because they have completed or are undergoing closure under State law; State requirements operate in lieu of Federal regulations only where the State program has been approved pursuant to RCRA section 4005(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To rely on State requirements in place of the Federal rule, the State must obtain EPA approval of its CCR permit program per the statute. In the absence of an approved State permit program, Federal criteria apply. EPA found insufficient record evidence to justify a broad exemption for closures under general State authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure options and obligation to meet §257.102 performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure of a CCR landfill or surface impoundment must be completed either by leaving the CCR in place and installing a final cover system (closure with waste in place) or through removal of the CCR and decontamination of the unit, as described in §257.102(b)–(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators may select either clean closure or closure with waste in place, but must meet all performance standards applicable to the chosen option. If a facility cannot meet the performance standards for one option (or portion of a unit), it must meet all the performance standards for the other option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-specific determination of ability to meet performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a particular unit or facility can meet the performance standards is a fact- and site-specific determination depending on hydrogeology, engineering of the unit, and the engineering measures available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should be based on factual and engineering considerations (e.g., whether unit intersects the aquifer, saturation, structural stability). EPA will assess these factors when determining appropriate closure measures or need for reclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral eligibility — oversight by a regulatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for deferral to permitting as potentially equivalent, the closure must have had active oversight and approval by a regulatory authority (State or Federal permit, an administrative order, or consent order issued after 2015 under CERCLA or by an EPA‑approved RCRA State program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulatory authority must have required groundwater monitoring to ensure no contamination was coming from the unit that was not addressed by corrective action. EPA considers this active oversight a prerequisite for deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral eligibility — elimination of free liquids (§257.102(d)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For closures that closed with waste in place, the facility must document that free liquids have been eliminated consistent with the standard in §257.102(d)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elimination of free liquids directly addresses EPA's concern about previously completed closures where saturated CCR or free liquids remained; documentation must show compliance with the cited standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral eligibility — adequate groundwater monitoring system (subset of §257.91(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The facility must document that it installed and operated a groundwater monitoring system capable of: (1) accurately representing background water quality; (2) accurately representing the quality of water passing the waste boundary; and (3) detecting contamination in the uppermost aquifer; and that the system monitored all potential contaminant pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the same subset of standards that apply to facilities certifying prior closure-by-removal. Documentation should show monitoring design, well locations, sampling results, and evidence that monitoring covered all potential release pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral eligibility — site-specific risk assessment and enforceable oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: A site-specific human health and ecological risk assessment must have been conducted or approved by the regulatory authority prior to (or as part of) approving the closure, and the closure and any necessary corrective action must have been overseen by the regulatory authority pursuant to an enforceable requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The risk assessment and enforceable oversight demonstrate that risks were evaluated and addressed. Approval by the regulatory authority and enforceability are required elements to justify deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral eligibility — documentation and certification in applicability report/operating record (§257.102(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility seeking deferral must prepare and include documentation in the applicability report and operating record demonstrating it meets the deferral criteria; this documentation must be certified by the owner/operator or authorized representative using the same language in §257.102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation includes State permits/orders, monitoring data, risk assessments, corrective action records, and any third-party reports. Certification formalizes the claim of eligibility for deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit application review and outcomes for equivalency determination
rubrics_metrics.description: When a permit authority evaluates a deferred closure for equivalency, the facility must provide sufficient information (including groundwater contaminant data) for EPA or a Participating State Director to determine whether §257.102 standards have been met. If EPA determines closure meets the standard, it will issue a permit; if not, the owner/operator must submit a full operating permit application and the permitting authority will specify requirements necessary for compliance with §257.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The permit application process is the primary mechanism EPA will use to collect information (groundwater, soil, sampling/analytical data) and to make an equivalency determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of closure deadline for legacy CCR surface impoundments
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must initiate closure for legacy CCR surface impoundments no later than Monday, May 8, 2028 (42 months from the effective date of the final rule), except for units eligible for deferral (e.g., closed under State authority or beneath critical infrastructure). (Codified at §257.101(e)(1).)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extension from the originally proposed 12 months accommodates time to collect groundwater monitoring data and characterize hydrogeology. Initiation of closure is defined by taking steps necessary to implement the closure plan (see §257.102(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of initiation for units beneath critical infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the legacy CCR surface impoundment is beneath infrastructure vital to continued activities (e.g., a substation), initiation of closure will be deferred until the infrastructure is no longer needed or until closure of the facility, whichever is sooner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision balances protection with operational continuity and reliability; deferred initiation is limited to situations where mandatory initiation would cause more harm than benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of initiation of closure (§257.102(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure has been initiated once any steps necessary to implement the closure plan have been taken, including submitting an application for necessary State/agency permits or permit modifications and taking steps to comply with prerequisites to completing closure of a CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation of these implementation steps establishes the legal start of the closure timeline and compliance obligations tied to initiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of a written closure plan — content and deadline (§257.102(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must prepare a written closure plan describing whether closure will be accomplished by leaving CCR in place or by removal, including a narrative describing how closure will meet all performance standards, and a schedule for completing closure activities. Deadline: no later than Monday, November 8, 2027 (36 months from effective date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CCR is left in place, the plan must include a description of the final cover system and how it will meet performance standards; if the base intersects groundwater, the plan must discuss engineering measures to remove groundwater prior to cover installation; the plan must address how post-closure infiltration and releases will be controlled, minimized, or eliminated to the maximum extent feasible. The plan must be based on recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure-by-removal completion requires Appendix IV constituent confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure by removal completed prior to the effective date is considered complete only when documentation shows all Appendix IV constituent concentrations are below the Groundwater Protection Standard (GWPS) in two consecutive groundwater monitoring sampling events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures that removal closures are accompanied by confirmatory groundwater data showing contaminants are below regulatory limits; absence of such monitoring undermines claims of completed closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of a written post-closure care plan — content and deadline (§257.104(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must prepare a P.E.-certified written post-closure care plan describing monitoring and maintenance activities required for the unit, the frequency of those activities, point-of-contact for the post‑closure period, and planned uses of the property. Deadline: no later than Monday, November 8, 2027 (36 months from effective date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certified plan documents how the unit will be monitored and maintained during post-closure and is part of the facility's operating record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure completion timeframe and extension rules (§257.102(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of CCR surface impoundments must complete closure activities within five years from initiating closure. Documentation can support up to two-year extensions: impoundments ≤40 acres may receive one two‑year extension; impoundments >40 acres may receive two-year extensions in increments for up to five times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities seeking extensions must meet regulatory documentation requirements showing why additional time is necessary. EPA expects closure to be completed as promptly as practicable while allowing limited extensions for legitimate constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-closure care duration and requirements (§257.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Units that have closed with CCR in place must be monitored and maintained for at least 30 years after closure has been completed; during that period the facility must continue groundwater monitoring and corrective action where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-closure activities are essential to ensure long-term protection; the 30-year minimum may be supplemented by corrective action requirements if monitoring indicates contamination or risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrofit as potential alternative (consideration of §257.102(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA solicited comment on whether owners/operators should be allowed the option to retrofit a legacy CCR surface impoundment in accordance with retrofit requirements in §257.102(k) as an alternative to requiring closure of a legacy impoundment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No commenters provided sufficient feedback on permitting retrofits; EPA did not finalize a retrofit option as an alternative in this section, but the possibility was considered. Facilities should not assume retrofit is an approved alternative absent specific regulatory text permitting it.
